body.statement:
For each \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\), there are pairs
\[
(P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\subset
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)
\]
such that \(P_{\ell,q}(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\mid E_0)\ge c_X\), their conditional joint observed-data testing affinity is uniformly bounded away from zero,
\[
\inf_{N,T,\mathbf n}\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}>0,
\]
and
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,q}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,q}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cR_q
\quad\text{on }\mathcal Z_+,
\]
where \(R_q\) uses \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\) in the spacing channel.  The treated-mean, replicated-smoothing, and donor pairs may additionally be chosen with uniformly bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence.  For the random-spacing pair only positive testing affinity is asserted.  Every pair is induced by a regular conditional law of the complete causal panel; in particular, its event means are stable given the complete historical design and its historical errors are centered given that design.
body.justification: All four pairs are completed as causal panels in the enlarged full-design-centered subclass.
body.gap: No identical within-site response law or class-wide response-variance lower bound is used; the spacing experiment is certified by positive affinity rather than bounded divergence.
body.consumer: Both minimax and interval lower bounds apply to regular conditional causal-panel laws.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a regular conditional law given \(E_0\), and write
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\}.
\]
Choose all numerical constants in the nonempty interior of the fixed support, Holder, covariance, and modulus envelopes, and place the query in a fixed compact subset of \(\mathcal Z_+\) inside \(([0,1]^d)^S\).  In every experiment below, draw bounded event outcomes independently of \(\mathscr X\).  Conditional on \(\mathscr X\), draw bounded historical response paths independently across units from possibly heterogeneous kernels sharing the conditional mean \(m_s(X_{st})\).  It follows directly that
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{40}
\]
Complete the unobserved event-date untreated potential outcomes so that their cohort-average conditional means are \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  Set observed and historical potential outcomes according to consistency, make historical potential outcomes invariant to the event treatment, and make every potential outcome invariant to other units' assignments.  This verifies consistency, historical consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, and event transport.  Draw donors conditionally iid, independently of the panel, with covariance and standardized fourth moment strictly inside the declared envelopes, and set \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  Bounded response kernels, design laws, carriers, and donors are chosen as specified channel by channel below.  Thus (40) verifies exactly the two additional full-design restrictions, while identical within-site laws and a response-variance lower bound are not class requirements.

If \(p,p+v\in[\eta,1-\eta]\), Taylor's theorem applied to binary relative entropy gives
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p+v,p)\le\frac{v^2}{2\eta(1-\eta)}.
\tag{41}
\]
Conditional product structure makes the divergence of each response experiment the sum of these conditional binary divergences.

For the treated channel put \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\) and change the event response probability in cohort \(s\) by
\[
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}}.
\]
Since \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), \(|v_s|\le c_0n_s^{-1/2}\); sufficiently small fixed \(c_0\) keeps all probabilities in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).  The target separation and divergence satisfy
\[
\sum_s\pi_sv_s=c_0V_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}=c_0R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{tr}},P_{0,\mathrm{tr}})
\le C\sum_sn_sv_s^2=Cc_0^2.
\tag{42}
\]

For the smoothing channel choose \(s_*\) maximizing \(\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\), set \(b=(Tn_{s_*})^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\), and perturb only that cohort by
\[
m_{s_*,1}(x)-m_{s_*,0}(x)
=c_1b^\lambda\psi((x-z_{0s_*})/b),
\tag{43}
\]
where \(\psi\) is a fixed compactly supported \(\lambda\)-Holder bump with \(\psi(0)=1\).  Use a common affine carrier with nonzero covariance-standardized gradient when \(\lambda>1\), and a common asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp carrier when \(0<\lambda\le1\).  The increment calculation in the proof of \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}, with \(b\) in place of \(h_T\), shows that sufficiently small fixed \(c_1\) preserves the response interior, Holder radius, and both sides of the local-modulus inequality.  Because \(S\) is fixed,
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)|^2
=c_1^2\pi_{s_*}^2b^{2\lambda}\ge cR_{\mathrm{sm}}.
\tag{44}
\]
The design probability of the bump support is at most \(Cb^d\), so (41), integrated over the design and summed over the \(Tn_{s_*}\) observations, gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{sm}},P_{0,\mathrm{sm}})
\le CTn_{s_*}b^{2\lambda+d}=C.
\tag{45}
\]
An iid uniform design verifies the design-only mixing condition in this channel.

For the spacing channel take the pair constructed in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}.  It satisfies (40), the marginal density bounds, design-only geometric mixing, and the two-sided modulus.  Its observed laws coincide on a no-active-block event of probability bounded away from zero, and
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)|^2
\ge c\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}
=cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{46}
\]
Hence this pair has positive testing affinity; no Kullback--Leibler bound is asserted.

For the donor channel retain the same affine or asymmetric-cusp carrier.  By the lower local-modulus inequality, for \(\delta=c_2N^{-1/2}\le\delta_0\), the supremum in \texttt{def:local-modulus} supplies an admissible \(u_N\), chosen to attain at least half the supremum, such that
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2\le c_2N^{-1/2},
\qquad
\left|\sum_s\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{N,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\ge cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{47}
\]
Choose a fixed common-support finite distribution on \(\mathbb R^{Sd}\) whose support affinely spans \(\mathbb R^{Sd}\), whose covariance lies strictly inside the ellipticity envelope, and whose atom probabilities lie strictly inside the probability simplex.  Perturb those probabilities along a bounded score whose mean shift is \(u_N\).  The spanning property solves the finite linear mean equations, and interiority keeps all probabilities positive for sufficiently small \(c_2\).  Continuity preserves the covariance and fourth-moment envelopes.  Taylor expansion of the finite probability-vector likelihood, whose Hessian is bounded on this compact simplex neighborhood, yields
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{don}},P_{0,\mathrm{don}})
\le CN\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2\le Cc_2^2.
\tag{48}
\]
Keep the observed event mean fixed and complete untreated event potential outcomes under each law with cohort means equal to the corresponding surface at the corresponding donor mean.  The identifying equality in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} turns (47) into a target separation whose square is at least \(cR_{\mathrm{don}}\).

For any two laws, apply data processing to \(A=\{dP_1/dP_0\ge1\}\).  Twice differentiating binary relative entropy shows that it is at least twice the squared difference of the two event probabilities.  Hence
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)\ge2\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}^2,
\qquad
\int\min\{dP_0,dP_1\}
\ge1-\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2}.
\tag{49}
\]
Reducing \(c_0,c_1,c_2\) makes (49) uniformly positive for the treated, smoothing, and donor pairs; (46) supplies affinity directly for spacing.  The causal completions preceding (41) verify membership in the same enlarged full-design-centered class for all four pairs, proving every assertion.
